verdict: Berkshire's operating earnings slipped 6% to $10.1B as Hurricane Helene cut insurance underwriting to $750M — but $20.5B of investment gains lifted headline profit to $26.3B, a swing from a $12.8B loss a year ago, when the stock portfolio fell.

takeaways.title: Hurricanes hit underwriting
takeaways.text: After-tax underwriting earnings fell to $750M from $2,422M a year ago. Hurricane Helene alone cost about $715M in the reinsurance business and about $260M at GEICO before tax — while GEICO's premiums earned still grew about 5% on higher prices per policy.

takeaways.title: Paper gains swung the headline
takeaways.text: Headline profit swung from a $12.8B loss a year ago to $26.3B — almost entirely the stock portfolio. A year ago investment losses were $29.8B before tax; this quarter they were $20.5B of gains, including about $18.4B after tax realized on sales, mostly trimming Apple.

takeaways.title: The cash pile set another record
takeaways.text: Cash and Treasury Bills reached about $320B at September 30 — $32.3B of cash plus $288.0B of Treasury Bills — as Berkshire sold far more stock than it bought. Insurance float was about $174B.

oneTimers: Investment gains of $20,514M before tax ($16,161M after tax) are mostly paper gains. Of the after-tax total, about $18.4B was realized on sales of investments and $2.2B was unrealized losses on stocks Berkshire still owns. Next quarter the unrealized part can just as easily reverse — a year ago this line was a $29,778M pre-tax loss.

Hurricane Helene struck in late September: roughly $715M of pre-tax losses in the reinsurance group and about $260M at GEICO. After-tax insurance underwriting earnings fell to $750M from $2,422M a year ago.

Currency moves on foreign debt: revaluing Berkshire's euro-, pound- and yen-denominated borrowings produced a loss of about $1.1B after tax inside the 'Other' operating earnings line, versus a gain of about $447M a year ago.

sources.label: Form 10-Q, quarter ended September 30, 2025 — reclassified 2024 comparatives (SEC EDGAR)
